findings.title: Embedded-post author link uses the wrong lightness
findings.body: This rule previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement uses 70% for the primary branch and 30% for the secondary branch. That reverses the intended dark-theme color and also changes the light-theme color, making these author links substantially lighter than before.

findings.title: Custom-message length color has reversed lightness values
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; the replacement uses 30% for the primary branch and 70% for the secondary branch. This reverses the intended lightness in both theme branches, so the character-count text will render with the wrong contrast.

findings.title: Topic-map heading no longer preserves its original lightness
findings.body: This heading previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but both branches now use 50%. The change makes the heading much lighter in light themes and fails to use the intended 80%-lightness secondary color in dark themes, reducing the intended theme contrast.

findings.title: Group-member name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original name color used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement uses 50% for both theme branches. This changes the name color in light themes and does not provide the intended 70%-lightness secondary color in dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile group-member name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original name color used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement uses 50% for both theme branches. This changes the name color in light themes and does not provide the intended 70%-lightness secondary color in dark themes.
